body.statement: For every \(\ell\) and every admissible \(\rho,c\), \(\log H(r_{\ell1},r_{\ell2},r_{\ell3})-\log(\rho Q_{\ell})=A_{\ell}B_{\rho,\ell}\), \(B_{\rho,\ell}<0\), and \(\Delta_{\ell}-\Delta^P_{\ell}=\rho Q_{\ell}A_{\ell}C_{\rho,\ell}\) with \(C_{\rho,\ell}<0\). Consequently, \(\Delta_{\ell}=\Delta^P_{\ell}\) if and only if \(c_{\ell1}=c_{\ell3}\) or \(c_{\ell2}=c_{\ell3}\).
body.justification: The factorization exposes the entire cancellation geometry and leaves no additive remainder on either plane.
body.gap: Pinelis and Baricz control one-dimensional Mills objects; neither derives this mixed DiD identity or its exact two-plane zero set.
body.consumer: Researchers comparing normal-link and proportional-effect DTTs obtain an observable coefficient geometry that tells when link choice is exactly immaterial.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(\ell\) and suppress its index.  Set \(b=\rho c_3\), \(x=\log(c_1/c_3)\), \(z=\log(c_2/c_3)\), and
\[
R_b(x,z)=\log\Phi\{q(be^x)+q(be^z)-q(b)\}-\log b-x-z.
\]
The coefficient and rarity assumptions imply that every probability appearing here or on the line segments below belongs to \((0,1)\).  Since \(q'(p)=1/\phi(q(p))\) and \(p=\Phi(q(p))\),
\[
\frac{d}{da}q(be^a)=\frac{be^a}{\phi(q(be^a))}
=\frac{1}{m(q(be^a))}.
\]
Writing \(S=q(be^x)+q(be^z)-q(b)\), two ordinary differentiations give
\[
\partial_{xz}R_b(x,z)
=\frac{m'(S)}{m(q(be^x))m(q(be^z))}.
\]
Moreover \(R_b(x,0)=R_b(0,z)=0\) exactly.  The two-dimensional fundamental theorem of calculus on the signed rectangle from \((0,0)\) to \((x,z)\) consequently gives
\[
R_b(x,z)=xz\int_0^1\!\int_0^1
 \frac{m'\{q(be^{sx})+q(be^{tz})-q(b)\}}
 {m(q(be^{sx}))m(q(be^{tz}))}\,dt\,ds
=A B_\rho.
\]
This formula remains valid when either side of the signed rectangle is zero; no division by \(x\), \(z\), or \(A=xz\) has occurred.

Direct differentiation of \(m=\phi/\Phi\) yields
\[
m'(v)=-m(v)\{v+m(v)\}.
\]
For \(v\ge0\), the bracket is positive.  For \(v=-a<0\), \(a>0\),
\[
\Phi(-a)=\phi(a)\int_0^\infty e^{-at-t^2/2}\,dt
<\phi(a)\int_0^\infty e^{-at}\,dt=\frac{\phi(a)}a,
\]
so \(m(-a)>a\), and the bracket is again positive.  Thus \(m'(v)<0\) for every real \(v\).  All denominator factors in the integral are positive, whence \(B_\rho<0\).

By common rarity, \(be^x=\rho c_1\), \(be^z=\rho c_2\), and \(be^{x+z}=\rho Q\).  Exponentiating the identity for \(R_b\) gives
\[
H(r_1,r_2,r_3)=\rho Q e^{AB}.
\]
Therefore, using \(e^w-1=w\psi(w)\),
\[
\Delta-\Delta^P
=H(r_1,r_2,r_3)-\rho Q
=\rho Q A B\psi(AB)
=\rho Q A C_\rho.
\]
The integral definition of \(\psi\) shows \(\psi(w)>0\) for every real \(w\); hence \(C_\rho=B\psi(AB)<0\).  Since \(\rho Q>0\) and \(C_\rho\ne0\), equality \(\Delta=\Delta^P\) is equivalent to \(A=xz=0\), which is equivalent to \(c_1=c_3\) or \(c_2=c_3\).
